'''Edward Blades''' was a Scottish mathematician and teacher. He later became the [[West Lothian]] Director of Education and was awarded an [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] for army education services during the [[World War II|Second World War]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Edward Blades - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Blades/ |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Page 1 {{!}} Supplement 38161, 30 December 1947 {{!}} London Gazette {{!}} The Gazette |url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/London/issue/38161/supplement/1 |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=www.thegazette.co.uk}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Edward Blades was the youngest child of Daniel and Janet Blades on 6 March 1875 in [[Armadale, West Lothian|Armadale]] [[Scotland]]. His father was a blacksmith. He attended Armadale Public School, where he later taught as a pupil teacher.<ref name=":0" />  

He attended the [[University of Edinburgh]] from 1894 to 1900, graduating with a [[Master of Arts (Scotland)|MA]] in [[Mathematics]] and [[Natural philosophy|Natural Philosophy]]. He was later awarded a B.S.c (Pure) in 1902.<ref name=":0" />  

After university, Blades attended the Training College and received a Diploma of Education at the Higher Grade as well as the Kelland memorial prize, the Ramsay memorial prize, and six additional medals.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |title=Retiring Educationist Honoured: Lothians Career of Mr Edward Blades |pages=13 |work=[[The Scotsman]] |url=https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0000540/19391216/115/0013 |access-date=2023-06-21}}</ref>  

== Career ==
Blades was the junior lecturer in [[Mathematics]] and Science and [[Geography]] assistant at [[Moray House School of Education and Sport|Moray House Training College]]. He also lectured honours [[Geology]] at [[Heriot-Watt University|Heriot-Watt College]]. He then became the head of [[George Watson's College|George Watson's Ladies' College]] mathematics department. In 1905 he joined the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]].<ref name=":0" /> From 1919, he was the Executive Officer to [[West Lothian]] Education Authority until 1930 when he became the Director of Education for the West Lothian Education Committee (precursors to the current West Lothian Council.)<ref name=":2" /> He retired from this post in 1939. He was then appointed the secretary of the Edinburgh University extra Mural Committee.<ref name=":0" />

During World War 2, although retired, Blades championed the ''University Extra-Mural Committee'' for civilian adult education.<ref name=":0" /> For his service he was awarded an honorary [[Bachelor of Laws|Bachelors of Law]] from the University of Edinburgh as well as an [[1948 New Year Honours|O.B.E. (Civil Division)]] for Army Education services in 1948.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite news |date=1954-01-08 |title="Obituaries" |pages=5 |work=West Lothian Courier |url=https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002738/19540108/050/0005?browse%20=%20false |access-date=2023-06-21}}</ref>  

Blades died in an Edinburgh nursing home on 21 November 1953.<ref name=":3" />
